Incorporating the Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey around the May 2018 meeting:
- C&I lending: Standards were generally unchanged to modestly easier (especially for large and middle-market firms), with stronger loan demand. Banks often cited competition as the driver of easing. This supports the FOMC’s read of strong business fixed investment and a still-solid growth backdrop.
- CRE lending: Standards tightened on net and demand softened, a drag that aligns with a more cautious stance on sectors sensitive to late-cycle risks.
- Residential mortgages and consumer credit: Mortgage standards eased somewhat in certain segments while consumer lending standards and demand were largely unchanged, consistent with the FOMC’s observation that household spending had moderated from its strong Q4 pace.

Net take: SLOOS corroborates a constructive macro tone (business activity and employment) while reinforcing financial-stability caution (competition-driven easing in some business credit, tighter CRE). That mix nudges the overall tone slightly more cautious than a pure macro read, but still moderately positive.
